messages:
maria: We're seeing a short spike around 13:02 UTC that caused a flurry of 429s for one of our endpoints. Happened after a CI job kicked off ~45 parallel inference calls. Example log: "request_id=abc123 status=429". Anyone know if burst credits should've prevented this?

sam_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact request pattern? burst credits are intended for brief spikes but they can be exhausted if concurrency is high.

maria: Repro: ran a loop with 50 concurrent curl calls to POST /v1/generate over ~10s. Each request uses ~300 tokens. Auth is via API key on the hosted plan. No prior heavy traffic that hour.

luis_eng: Quick notes from infra: burst credits (our short-term smoothing cushion) are consumed per-token/per-request depending on route, and they refill gradually. If your concurrency consumes them faster than they refill, you'll hit rate limits until the cushion recovers. The 429 will include a Retry-After and remaining-quota headers — use those for backoff.

sam_support: For immediate mitigation, try:
- reduce concurrency to ~10-15 while you smooth the traffic
- add jittered exponential backoff reading Retry-After
- shard requests across multiple API keys if you can (temporary)
- enable the per-route smoothing policy in Console (Settings → Rate controls)

maria: Is there a setting we can flip now to 'spread' the 50 requests so they don't all land at once?

luis_eng: Two options: 1) client-side shaping (add small random delays before requests), 2) enable smoothing in Console which will queue and pace requests at the edge to avoid exhausting the cushion. Smoothing trades a tiny ephemeral latency increase for fewer 429s.

opsbot: deploy-bot: rolling update to rate-limiter config completed at 13:04 UTC (no errors).

sam_support: If you want we can temporarily bump your smoothing aggressiveness for that route while you re-architect the job — ping with the route name and team account id.

maria: Route is /v1/generate, account=ac-9f2. I tried client-side jitter and it helped, but would like smoothing enabled as well. Thanks!

luis_eng: Filed a quick internal task to enable stronger smoothing for ac-9f2 on /v1/generate for 6 hours. I'll post the change id here once applied.

sam_support: Also sending a short guide (copy below) you can use for CI: 

```
# pseudo-wrapper
parallel=20
for i in $(seq 1 $parallel); do
  sleep $(python -c "import random; print(random.random()*0.5)")
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{...}' &
done
wait
```

maria: awesome, that snippet is perfect. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:

luis_eng: change applied: cfg-2026-31. Monitor headers and tell us if 429s persist.

maria: All green now, no more 429s after config change. Thanks everyone! :tada:
